pageCache.pageTitle: School Improvement Fund | Ashford Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
School Improvement Fund (also known as Buildings and Maintenance Fund)
As you may already be aware Church schools receive funding for buildings in a different way to community schools and we are reliant on the support of parents to help us fund the necessary building projects to provide the best possible learning environment for your children. We work closely with the Diocese who are responsible for large scale building projects.
For every £1 that is donated to the school for improvements to the building we can apply for another £9 of grant funding from the Diocese. Whilst parental donations are vital to allow us to make these improvements, these payments are voluntary as we recognise that family budgets are currently under pressure. In light of this we suggest the following amounts by way of a contribution:
As contributions are easy to forget, we would like to encourage as many of you as possible to set up a standing order, enclosed you will find the relevant form to complete and return to the school office. You can also pay online via our Tucasi payment service, by cash or by cheque (made payable to “Ashford C/E B & M Fund”). Our staff in the office will be happy to assist you in any way they can. We have also included a Gift Aid form for you to complete if you are a UK tax payer. This means we receive an additional 25p for every £1 donated.
Our staff team at ACE are always striving to make improvements to the learning environment and continue to come up with practical and exciting ideas so that we can maximise the potential of the space for your children. We have many exciting plans and aspirations for future improvements, so please keep giving anything you can so we can make these ideas a reality.
School Improvement Letter
Over the Easter holidays in 2025 we made some important changes to our Reception class rooms, which included new floors, a new sliding door to partition Kangaroo class to provide separate teaching spaces for the children and full redecoration. The classes look fantastic and the children are enjoying the flexible class room spaces. Staff are seeing great benefits to the children’s learning already, with quieter spaces for the development of the children’s reading and phonics skills. None of this would be possible without the support of our families

Our Governors
Provide a strategic view which sets out and continuously reviews the broad framework within which the headteacher and staff run the school. The focus is on:
Act as a critical friend by giving advice and support and fostering good relationships. They ask challenging and critical questions and strive for improvements. Ensure accountability by setting out the overall aims and conduct for the school, approving policies and plans to support this.
The headteacher and staff report to the governors on the school’s performance. Proposals are discussed, questioned and refined, with regard to the professional roles of the staff and their day to day responsibilities within the school. The governors are also answerable for their actions to the Local Authority and the London Diocesan Board of School.
Raising standards of achievement
Promoting effective teaching and learning

pageCache.text:
Governors
Governors are a very special group of people who help direct and support the school’s educational and pastoral activities. The Governing Body has many strategic functions, as Ashford CE Primary is a voluntary aided school they also have a responsibility to maintain and develop the premises.
Historically Ashford school’s governors are parents, ex parents and long-standing pillars of our Christian community. We also have Foundation governors, appointed through the PCC of our parish churches. Together with the school’s senior leadership team, the governors are focusing their involvement on enhancing teaching and learning throughout the school. Our governing body has adopted a code of conduct to uphold the seven principles of public life: selflessness, integrity, objectivity, accountability, openness, honesty and leadership.
Minutes of Full Governing Body (FGB) meetings are available on request from the Clerk of Governors via the school office.
Attendance
Governor Attendance 2024/25
Committees
We currently have the following committees that meet as and when required:
Chair Jenny Wilsher. The responsibility of the Committee is to:
Chair Jenny Wilsher. This committee has delegated responsibility from the Full Governing Body (FGB) to carry out the required admissions processes for the school.
Chair Louise Bowman. This committee has delegated responsibility from the Full Governing Body (FGB) to carry out the performance management process for the Headteacher on an annual basis.
Chair Louise Bowman. This committee focuses on the achievement of the school’s aims and in respect of all pay matters. Specifically ensuring staff are appropriately rewarded for their performance in line with the pay policy.
In 2016 the Governing Body decided to adopt a new model for meetings instead of delegating some tasks to committees they now meet 11 times a year. This streamlined approach enables the Governing Body to concentrate on the aim of raising standards on the drive to “Outstanding”.
Monitor and evaluate assessment for all groups.
Meetings
The Governing Body of Ashford CE Primary School has agreed that Full Governing Body meetings will be “open.” Open meetings are meetings of the Full Governing Body to which members of the public, including school staff and parents can request, in writing, to attend, as observers. This protocol outlines the conduct expected by the governing body of those requesting attendance.

Inspection Reports
All schools are the subject of independent inspections from the Government’s Office for Standards in Education (Ofsted) and Church of England schools have a further inspection (SIAMS) by The National Society.
Following our most recent Ofsted inspection (September 2023), we would like to draw your attention to these particular feedback points: “Pupils are proud to be a part of this happy and inclusive school.” “Pupils behave very well and respect their peers and adults. Lessons are calm and purposeful.” “The school actively promotes personal development and well- being.” “Pupils value difference and they celebrate diversity.” “Since the last inspection, the school has put in place a well-planned and ambitious curriculum across every subject.” “Parents speak positively about the changes that have happened across the school and feel part of a cohesive school community.”
Please follow the links on this page to the most recent published reports.

Parent Teacher Association
Welcome to the Ashford C of E Primary School PTA!
Our Parent Teacher Association (PTA) is a vibrant and welcoming part of school life, bringing together parents, carers, teachers, and staff to enhance the educational experience of every child at Ashford C of E Primary.
The PTA works throughout the year to support our school community. We:
Why Your Support Matters
Every parent and carer is automatically part of the PTA, and there are many ways to get involved – from helping at events to sharing ideas or offering a bit of your time. Every contribution, big or small, makes a real difference.
By supporting the PTA, you are helping to enrich the learning environment for all our children – and it’s a great way to meet other families and be part of school life.
If you’d like to find out more, volunteer, or share your ideas, we’d love to hear from you ashfordcofepta@gmail.com
Together, we can make a positive and lasting impact on our children’s primary school journey.
PTA Letters
Easyfundraising Poster
PTA Policies and Procedures
The policy and procedure below has been compiled by the PTA for its members, active members of the committee and Trustees. It gives more in-depth explanation about the PTA, safety and procedural policies which are required for Charity organisations. If you have any questions that remain unanswered, please contact one of the committee members (Co-Chairs, Treasurer or Secretary) via the school office or speak to a member of school staff.
PTA Policies and Procedures
Fundraising
We would like to say a huge thank you to our school community for their support which has enabled us to fund and contribute to projects and activities at school.
If your children enjoy the events, and the equipment we’ve been able to provide for them please consider how YOU can help in the future! We are always looking for active committee members but would welcome any help you are able to give. If everyone helped, even in a small way it would both enable our activities to continue and help enhance your children’s time at Ashford CE Primary School.
